source.title: On the Asymptotic Learning Curves of Kernel Ridge Regression under Power-law Decay
source.authors: Yicheng Li; Hao Zhang; Qian Lin

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices and experiments, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper provides its own theoretical and experimental KRR learning curves, arguing that noisy KRR has a U-shaped curve in the regularization parameter while noiseless KRR is monotone decreasing. This refines or challenges the general double-descent account, though it does not sweep neural-network size or training epochs.
record.gate_note: The study tests KRR learning curves as regularization changes, including the near-interpolating regime. Its results are about KRR and regularization, not neural-network size or training epochs. Cited double-descent results are not recorded as findings. The experimental table reports estimated asymptotic rates, not test-error values.
record.test_reason: The paper derives and checks KRR excess-risk curves as regularization shrinks toward interpolation, in fixed input dimension. It argues the curve is the classical U-shape with noise, and that noisy kernel interpolation cannot generalize. This is a specific argument against benign overfitting and a second descent in this setting. It sweeps the regularization strength, not parameter count, so it bears on V4 and V6 only indirectly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that KRR risk is U-shaped in the regularization parameter with noise and monotone decreasing without noise, which matches the classical bias-variance trade-off. They also conclude that noisy kernel interpolation cannot generalize. Their stated implication is that benign overfitting in very wide (NTK-regime) networks exists only when noise is small.
record.recipe_differences: The study gives asymptotic KRR analyses and toy KRR experiments, rather than reproducing the original deep-network capacity sweeps. It varies regularization and studies noise and source smoothness.
record.method_sensitivity: The curve depends on whether observations are noisy or noiseless; rates also depend on regularization exponent θ, source smoothness s, eigenvalue decay β, and noise level σ². In the appendix, the stated crossover in sample-size curves occurs earlier with larger noise and smoother target functions.

fits_no_version.finding: Noisy fixed-dimension kernel interpolation has a non-vanishing excess risk, so benign overfitting fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolating kernel estimators in fixed dimension with noisy labels are inconsistent: no benign overfitting.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (2023); the text also labels the paper a preprint under review.
record.problems: The theoretical conclusions depend on the stated kernel, source, embedding, and noise assumptions. Experiments use a toy one-dimensional kernel setting and estimated asymptotic rates; they do not directly evaluate neural-network model-size double descent. Some nearly interpolating bounds are lower bounds or upper bounds rather than matching exact rates.

untested.parts: No test of whether more samples raise error near a threshold; n is varied only to fit rates.
No sweep of parameter count past n; only regularization in fixed-dimension KRR; no other model classes.
No effective-complexity predictor of peak location.
No test of multiple or triple peaks. Disappearance of a peak under optimal regularization is not tested as such, since there is no peak to remove.
No re-parameterization by an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Kernel interpolation (λ=0) learning curves across noise levels, showing excess risk not decaying with n under noise.
Learning curves across noise levels at θ=1 and θ=2, showing the noisy-to-noiseless crossover occurs at smaller n when noise is larger.
Variance-term rates, which are near 0 for θ≥2 and show variance not decaying in the interpolating regime.

record.verdict_notes: The axis is the regularization exponent θ at fixed input dimension, not parameter count, so links to V4 are indirect. The paper cites Belkin et al. 2019 (an original source) only as background; the study itself is not an original source. Table 1 rows are rate verifications across n and are relinked to none.

versions.untested_parts: No deep-network model-size sweep or test-error curve over model size.
The paper varies sample size in experiments but does not test whether increasing sample size raises error near an interpolation threshold.
Tests KRR through regularization rather than explicit capacity sweeps; does not test deep networks or a range of other model classes.
Does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Tests noisy versus noiseless settings and regularization dependence. Does not test multiple or triple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization makes a peak disappear.
Does not re-express the curve using an effective parameter count or test whether that produces an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: Kernel ridge regression (KRR)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical excess-risk rate as regularization decreases with λ ≍ n^-θ, for 0 < θ < β.

conditions.value: Assumptions 1–5; source smoothness s and eigenvalue decay β

rows.value: Θ̃P(n^-min(s,2)θ + σ² n^-(1-θ/β)); ΘP can replace Θ̃P if s ≠ 2.
rows.uncertainty: Asymptotic probabilistic rate bounds, as stated
rows.note: The two terms are identified as bias and variance. The authors describe the noisy regularization curve as U-shaped; this is a KRR regularization result, not a direct model-size sweep.

source_check.correct: V4: cannot_determine; the regularization sweep does not measure capacity beyond interpolation. V6: observed for the noise-dependent overfitting rise. The stated excess-risk rate is correct.
source_check.problem: Observed conflates the noise-dependent rise with V4's renewed improvement beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: Kernel ridge regression (KRR)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical excess-risk bound in the nearly interpolating regime λ ≍ n^-θ, θ ≥ β.
rows.uncertainty: Asymptotic probabilistic lower bound, as stated
rows.note: The authors describe this regime as having a near-constant lower bound and state that kernel interpolation cannot generalize in the noisy case. The result does not show a second descent beyond interpolation.
rows.check: Absent refers to V4: there is no improvement at the interpolating end, since risk is bounded below by a near-constant Ω(σ²). For V6 the same row shows the noise-driven rise at interpolation as observed. The value is a lower bound only.

source_check.correct: V4: cannot_determine. V6: observed for persistent noise-dependent error near interpolation. The bound is Ω_P^poly(σ²), which establishes nonvanishing asymptotic risk up to subpolynomial factors, rather than a capacity curve beyond interpolation.
source_check.problem: Absent is not established for V4's capacity-dependent effect and does not describe the observed noise dependence under V6.

rows.subject: Kernel ridge regression (KRR)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical excess-risk rate as regularization decreases with λ ≍ n^-θ, for 0 < θ < β.
rows.value: Θ̃P(n^-min(s,2)θ); ΘP can replace Θ̃P if s ≠ 2.
rows.uncertainty: Asymptotic probabilistic rate bounds, as stated
rows.note: The authors state that the noiseless learning curve is monotone decreasing as θ increases in this regime.

source_check.correct: V4: cannot_determine. V6: observed for the disappearance of the overfitting rise without noise. The stated noiseless rate is correct.
source_check.problem: Monotone improvement toward interpolation does not establish V4's improvement beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: Kernel ridge regression (KRR)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical bias bound in the nearly interpolating regime λ ≍ n^-θ, θ ≥ β.
rows.measure: Expected excess risk (variance vanishes; risk equals bias squared)
rows.uncertainty: Asymptotic probabilistic upper bound, as stated
rows.note: This is an upper bound, not an exact rate. The authors state that the noiseless error continues decreasing and reaches the optimal rate when s ≤ 2; for s > 2, saturation limits the rate.
rows.check: This is an upper bound, but the authors state that noiseless error keeps decreasing to the optimal rate for s≤2 (Remark 3.5). So the noiseless monotone curve is observed, not partial. Saturation for s>2 limits only the rate.

source_check.correct: V4: cannot_determine. V6: observed for the noiseless contrast. For s > 1 and θ ≥ β, risk equals bias squared and has upper bound O_P^poly(n^-min(s,2)β).
source_check.problem: The noiseless upper bound and stated monotone regularization curve do not establish a second descent along capacity beyond interpolation.

relationships.condition: Noisy KRR in fixed dimension under Assumptions 1–5, swept along regularization λ≍n^-θ
relationships.reason: Risk follows a U-shape in θ (R1), and in the nearly interpolating regime it stays bounded below by Ω(σ²) (R2). There is no renewed improvement at the interpolating end in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Risk was U-shaped in θ and remained bounded below by Ω(σ²) near interpolation, without renewed improvement.

source_check.condition: Noisy KRR in fixed dimension under Assumptions 1–5, swept along regularization λ≍n^-θ
source_check.reason: R1–R2 establish a regularization curve and a nearly interpolating risk lower bound. They do not measure increasing capacity past interpolation; a nonvanishing lower bound alone also does not rule out a decrease above that bound.

relationships.reason: Risk decreases monotonically toward interpolation, with no intermediate peak, and interpolation is optimal (R3, R4). Good interpolation holds, but without any double-descent shape.
relationships.display_finding: Risk decreased monotonically toward optimal interpolation without an intermediate peak.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R3–R4 describe improvement toward interpolation along regularization, without testing the capacity axis beyond interpolation required by V4.

relationships.condition: Noisy versus noiseless KRR along the regularization axis
relationships.reason: The error rise at interpolation appears only with noise (R1, R2) and is absent without noise (R3, R4). This matches the claim that noise or variance drives the overfitting rise, though here it is a rise without a second descent.
relationships.display_finding: Error rose at interpolation with noise and lacked that rise without noise, but showed no second descent.

relation.reason: Its own theoretical results and toy experiments test noise and regularization dependence, bearing directly on V6.

tranche.reason: The paper explicitly argues against benign-overfitting interpretations in noisy fixed-dimensional KRR and derives conditions governing interpolation risk.

source_check.notes: Nearly interpolating noisy risk has a lower bound, not a proved exact constant rate. Remark 3.5 prints n^-β as the optimal noiseless rate, whereas Eqs. (17)–(18) give n^-sβ for 1 < s ≤ 2.

statements.correction: Fixed-dimensional KRR: noisy excess risk is U-shaped along regularization; noiseless excess risk decreases toward interpolation; nearly interpolating noiseless bound requires s > 1; no capacity sweep beyond interpolation.
statements.problem: The description of this study's noisy and noiseless regularization curves is correct. Its classification as challenging V4 overstates what this axis establishes.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Noisy KRR under the paper's assumptions, as regularization enters the nearly interpolating regime
reader_labels.reason: The authors report a noisy U-shaped regularization curve and a near-constant lower bound for θ ≥ β, rather than a second descent past interpolation (R1–R2). This is evidence for KRR only, not for all model classes.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Noiseless KRR under the paper's assumptions
reader_labels.reason: The reported curve is monotone decreasing in the noiseless case, so the noisy overfitting behavior does not hold across noise conditions (R3–R4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: KRR with positive noise variance versus noiseless observations
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports a U-shaped regularization curve with noise and a monotone decreasing curve without noise (R1–R4). It does not test the proposed multiple-peak or optimally tuned-regularization parts.
